title: Brown butter banana pancakes
blurb: Uses the bananas nobody wants.
description: Speckled bananas, nutty brown butter and a batter you can mix in one bowl. Fluffy enough for a Saturday, quick enough for a Tuesday.
imageAlt: A stack of golden banana pancakes with syrup running down the sides
steps: Melt the butter in a small pan over a medium heat and keep it going until it foams, smells nutty and turns the colour of a hazelnut. Take it off the heat.
Mash the bananas in a big bowl until nearly smooth. Whisk in the egg, the milk and most of the brown butter.
Add the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt and stir until just combined. Lumps are fine; overmixing is not.
Heat a non-stick pan over a medium heat with a little of the leftover butter. Drop in spoonfuls of batter and cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear, then flip and cook for 1 minute more.
Keep the cooked ones warm under a tea towel while you finish the batch. Serve with maple syrup and any banana that survived.

title: Granola
blurb: Our big-batch version. Do not skimp on the maple syrup.
description: Our double batch of Cookie and Kate’s granola: 650g of oats, a proper pile of nuts, less oil than the original and the full amount of maple syrup, because 12 tablespoons was not sweet enough. Makes about 32 servings and keeps for a couple of weeks.
imageAlt: Big clumps of golden granola on a baking sheet

ingredients.name: walnuts and other nuts, roughly chopped
coconut or olive oil (the original uses 240ml, this is plenty)
maple syrup or honey (the full amount; 12 tbsp was not sweet enough)

steps: Heat the oven to 175°C and line two large, rimmed baking sheets with baking paper.
In a very large bowl, mix the oats, nuts, salt and cinnamon.
Pour in the oil, maple syrup and vanilla and stir until every oat and nut is coated. Divide between the two trays and spread into an even layer.
Bake for 21 to 24 minutes until lightly golden, stirring halfway and swapping the trays between shelves. Press the granola back down after stirring if you want big clumps. It crisps up as it cools.
Leave to cool completely without touching it, at least 45 minutes, then add the dried fruit and break into clusters.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to two weeks, or freeze for up to three months.

title: Zucchini pesto pasta
blurb: Courgettes, pesto and penne in about half an hour.
description: Courgettes cooked until just tender, folded through pesto and penne with a splash of the pasta water. Dinner in about half an hour, and it takes any short pasta you have.
imageAlt: Penne tossed with pesto and sliced zucchini, topped with grated parmesan

ingredients.name: salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil with about 2 tsp of salt.
Trim the zucchini, halve them lengthways and slice into half-moons. Measure out the pesto and mince the garlic.
Cook the pasta in the boiling water until just al dente. Before draining, scoop out 120ml of the cooking water.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a very large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the garlic and cook for about a minute, until you can smell it. Do not let it brown.
Add the zucchini, season with salt and pepper and cook for about 5 minutes, until tender with a little bite.
Stir the pesto through the zucchini, then add the drained pasta and enough of the cooking water to bring everything together. Cook for a couple of minutes more so the pasta takes on the pesto.
Serve hot with the parmesan on top. Keeps in the fridge for a day or two.

title: Baked feta salmon pasta
blurb: The baked feta pasta, with salmon. One dish, high protein.
description: Salmon fillets roasted on top of a block of feta and cherry tomatoes, which collapse into a creamy sauce. Spinach wilts in at the end and the penne gets tossed through. One dish and about 35 minutes.
imageAlt: Salmon fillets baked on a block of feta with cherry tomatoes, tossed with penne and spinach

ingredients.name: penne, cooked al dente (keep a little of the cooking water)

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Put the feta, cherry tomatoes and salmon in a 23x33cm baking dish. Drizzle with the olive oil and scatter over the oregano, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the salmon is cooked through and flakes easily and the tomatoes have burst.
Take the dish out and add the spinach straight in. Leave it for 2 to 3 minutes to wilt.
Flake the salmon with a fork and mash the feta and tomatoes together until creamy, then stir everything into a sauce.
Add the cooked penne and toss until coated. Loosen with 2 to 3 tablespoons of the pasta water if it needs it.

title: Creamy roasted eggplant and tomato pasta
blurb: Silky, smoky, and all made in one pan.
description: Whole eggplant, tomatoes and garlic cooked down under a lid until they collapse, mashed into a smoky sauce with oat cream, chilli crisp and vegan parmesan, then tossed with linguine. Throw a zucchini into the pan too if you have one.
imageAlt: Linguine in a creamy, smoky roasted eggplant and tomato sauce topped with chilli crisp and parsley

ingredients.name: salt (plus a pinch for the cut surfaces)
oat cream or any vegan cream

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep pan over a medium heat. Put the eggplant halves in cut side down and sprinkle the cut surfaces with a pinch of salt. Add the tomatoes, the garlic cloves and the zucchini, if using. Cover and cook for 20 to 25 minutes until everything is completely soft and collapsing, turning the eggplant halfway if needed.
Use tongs to pull away the tomato and eggplant skins and discard them. Mash everything together in the pan with a potato masher or fork until you have a thick, chunky sauce.
Add the salt, pepper, smoked paprika, red pepper flakes, chili crisp, and vegan parmesan. Stir everything together and let it simmer for a couple of minutes.
Pour in the oat cream and stir until the sauce turns creamy and everything is well combined. Let it bubble gently for 2 to 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the linguine in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve some pasta water before draining.
Add the cooked pasta directly into the sauce and toss to coat. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of pasta water to loosen it up until every strand is coated.
Plate up and finish with extra vegan parmesan and fresh chopped parsley.

title: Blueberry banana muffins
blurb: Banana, peanut butter and oats. No flour, no fuss.
description: Fifteen muffins from one bowl: mashed banana and peanut butter for the body, oats and a heaped spoon of baking powder for lift, blueberries throughout. About 6g of protein each.
imageAlt: Two blueberry muffins with crumb topping stacked on a board, scattered with fresh blueberries
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line muffin tins with 15 paper cases.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl, then beat in the eggs, peanut butter and maple syrup until smooth.
Stir in the oats and baking powder, then fold in the blueberries.
Divide between the cases and bake for 25 minutes, until risen and golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes. They keep for 3 days in a tin, or freeze.

title: High-protein salmon toast
blurb: Mix, pile on toast, done. About 30g of protein a serve.
description: Flaked salmon, avocado, Greek yoghurt and cucumber with a squeeze of citrus, mixed in one bowl and piled onto toast or a baked sweet potato. Makes two generous serves.
imageAlt: Seeded toast topped with smashed avocado, flaked grilled salmon, feta and chives on a plate with a lemon wedge

ingredients.name: hot sauce and fresh dill, optional
bread, toasted, or 2 baked sweet potatoes

steps: Flake the salmon into a bowl. Dice the cucumber and avocado and add them with the yoghurt and citrus juice.
Season with salt and pepper, add hot sauce and dill if you like, and mix until creamy.
Pile half the mixture onto two slices of toast, or a baked sweet potato, per serve.

title: Honey garlic chicken marinade
blurb: Soy, honey, ginger and garlic. Sticky, glossy, and it caramelises on the grill.
description: A sticky soy and honey marinade with grated garlic, ginger and smoked paprika. Enough for about 700g of chicken. Thirty minutes minimum, overnight is where the magic happens. Brush the leftover marinade on at the end so the honey chars rather than burns.
imageAlt: Glossy honey garlic chicken breasts in a pan of sticky sauce, sprinkled with parsley
steps: Whisk everything together in a bowl or a zip bag.
Add about 700g of chicken thighs or breast, turn to coat, and marinate for at least 30 minutes. Overnight is best.
Cook however you like: grill, pan-fry, or roast at 200°C for 20 to 25 minutes until cooked through. Brush the marinade on towards the end so the honey does not burn.

title: Lemon garlic herb chicken marinade
blurb: Olive oil, a whole lemon, five cloves of garlic and dried herbs. Bright and clean.
description: Olive oil, the juice and zest of a whole lemon, plenty of garlic and a spoon each of Dijon and honey, with dried herbs to round it out. Enough for about 700g of chicken. Thirty minutes minimum, overnight is where the magic happens.
imageAlt: Raw chicken breasts on foil coated in lemon, garlic and chopped herbs, with lemon slices
steps: Whisk everything together in a bowl or a zip bag.
Add about 700g of chicken thighs or breast, turn to coat, and marinate for at least 30 minutes. Overnight is best.
Cook however you like: grill, pan-fry, or roast at 200°C for 20 to 25 minutes until cooked through.

title: Creamy chipotle lime chicken marinade
blurb: Greek yoghurt, chipotles in adobo and lime. Smoky, creamy, a little hot.
description: Greek yoghurt keeps the chicken tender while chipotles in adobo, lime and cumin bring smoke and heat. Enough for about 700g of chicken. Blend it if you want it smooth. Thirty minutes minimum, overnight is where the magic happens.
imageAlt: Chargrilled chipotle chicken breasts on a plate with lime wedges and coriander
steps: Whisk everything together in a bowl or a zip bag. Blend it if you want it smooth.
Add about 700g of chicken thighs or breast, turn to coat, and marinate for at least 30 minutes. Overnight is best.
Cook however you like: grill, pan-fry, or roast at 200°C for 20 to 25 minutes until cooked through.

title: Loaded sweet potato taco bowl
blurb: A roasted sweet potato, smashed, then piled high.
description: A whole sweet potato roasted until caramelised, smashed in a bowl and topped with seasoned beef mince, mozzarella, tomato, onion, jalapeños and avocado. A big single serve that keeps you full for hours.
imageAlt: Top-down view of a roasted sweet potato in a black bowl, loaded with beef mince, pico de gallo and a fan of sliced avocado with flaky salt
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Slice the sweet potato in half lengthways and season the cut sides with flaky salt.
Lay it cut side down on a lined baking tray and bake for about 40 minutes, until soft and caramelised.
While it cooks, brown the beef mince in a frying pan and season it to your liking.
Put both sweet potato halves in a bowl and smash the flesh gently with a fork to make a base.
Top with the mince, mozzarella, tomato, onion, jalapeños and avocado. Finish with the lime juice and a sprinkle of flaky salt.

title: Easy baked salmon
blurb: Lemon, garlic and herbs. On the table in 25 minutes.
description: Salmon fillets rubbed with olive oil, garlic, herbs and lemon juice, each topped with a slice of lemon and baked until just flaky. Finish under the grill for a minute if you like colour on top.
imageAlt: Three baked salmon fillets covered in herbs, with lemon slices, on a grey plate

ingredients.name: Italian herb seasoning (or ¼ tsp each of dried thyme, parsley, oregano and basil)
medium lemon, half juiced and half thinly sliced
fresh thyme or parsley, to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and grease a large baking dish. Arrange the salmon fillets in it and season generously with salt and pepper.
Stir together the olive oil, garlic, herbs and the juice of half the lemon. Spoon it over the salmon and rub it over the tops and sides so there are no dry spots.
Thinly slice the other half of the lemon and lay a slice on each fillet.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes when pulled with a fork. Grill for the last minute or two if you want colour on top.
Scatter with fresh thyme or parsley and serve.

title: Overnight oats
blurb: My one-jar version: oats and chia soaked in almond milk, banana for sweetness, peanut butter because it works.
description: Overnight oats the way I make them: a small jar of oats and chia soaked in almond milk, mashed banana for sweetness, a spoon of Greek yogurt for tang and protein, and peanut butter because it just goes. Stir it together before bed and breakfast is done. The amounts are for one jar; use the stepper to make a few for the week.
imageAlt: Four jars of overnight oats topped with apple and pecans, strawberries and peanut butter, peaches and granola, and banana with chocolate chips

ingredients.name: rolled oats (whole grain, the big flakes)
almond milk, plus a splash more (it soaks in overnight)
Greek yogurt (optional, adds tang and protein)
peanut butter (optional, but it goes so well)

steps: Put the oats, chia, salt, cinnamon and a little vanilla in a jar or a bowl with a lid.
Mash the banana and stir it in, along with the Greek yogurt and peanut butter if you are using them.
Pour in almond milk to cover, then a splash more: the oats and chia drink it up overnight and it should not end up dry. Stop before it turns thin. Stir well so no chia sits in clumps at the bottom.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for up to 5 days. Eat it cold in the morning, straight from the jar, with fruit or a drizzle of maple syrup on top if you like.

title: Creamy sausage pasta
blurb: Two kinds of sausage in a paprika cream sauce with melted mozzarella. Done in the time the pasta takes.
description: Sliced sausages, one cheese-filled and one frankfurter, browned and stirred into a quick paprika cream sauce with garlic and a pinch of curry powder, then mozzarella melted through and shells tossed in. It takes as long as the pasta takes to boil, which is why it shows up on busy weeknights.
imageAlt: Shell pasta and sliced sausages in an orange paprika cream sauce, a forkful lifted from a white bowl

ingredients.name: cheese-filled sausage (the kind stuffed with Dutch cheese), sliced

steps: Cook the pasta in well-salted water until just short of al dente. Scoop out 60ml of the cooking water before you drain it.
Meanwhile, brown the sliced sausages in a dry pan over medium-high heat until the edges catch, 3 to 4 minutes.
Turn the heat down, add the garlic, both paprikas, garlic powder, curry powder, pepper and salt, and stir for 30 seconds so the spices toast in the sausage fat.
Pour in the cream and the pasta water, bring to a simmer and let it thicken a little, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the mozzarella until it melts, then tip in the pasta and toss to coat. Loosen with a splash more pasta water if it tightens. Chilli flakes on top if you want heat.

title: Rolled egg breakfast wraps
blurb: Ugandan Rolex technique: a thin omelette cooked onto a tortilla, then filled with halloumi and roast veg. Freezer friendly.
description: Inspired by the Ugandan Rolex: a thin omelette cooked straight onto a tortilla, then filled with grated halloumi, roasted mushrooms and red onion, wilted spinach and hot sauce. Make four at once, wrap them, freeze them, and breakfast on the go is sorted for the week.
imageAlt: Three halved breakfast wraps in parchment, showing layers of omelette, mushrooms and spinach
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Thinly slice the mushrooms, cut each of the onions into eight wedges and place onto an oiled baking tray (you may need two trays). Season with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and cumin. Toss together and roast until golden and softened, 25-30 mins.

Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a bowl and season them with salt and garam masala. Whisk together. Pour boiling water over the spinach to wilt. Once cooled down a little, press down to squeeze out any excess water.

Place a frying pan, roughly the size of your tortillas onto medium heat with a drizzle of oil. Once hot, add just enough whisked eggs to cover the bottom of your pan, swirl around and let the bottom set. When the top of the omelette is still wet, place the tortilla on top, then flip. Toast the tortilla for a couple of seconds, then transfer to a plate. Continue this process until all the tortillas have been cooked.

Once the tortillas are done, finely grate the halloumi into a strip on one side of each omelette and cover with the roasted veggies, spinach and some hot sauce. Roll up the tortillas and wrap them in foil or parchment paper.

These rolled egg wraps can be eaten fresh or stored in the freezer until ready to eat. Reheat from frozen in the microwave until defrosted, or pan fry on medium-low until thawed and piping hot throughout.

title: Tzatziki
blurb: Greek yogurt, squeezed cucumber, garlic, lemon and dill. Fifteen minutes, keeps for days.
description: The classic Greek yogurt and cucumber sauce. The one trick is squeezing the grated cucumber dry so the dip stays thick. Makes about 600ml: enough to go with the chicken marinades, pile onto flatbreads, or eat with vegetables all week.
imageAlt: A patterned bowl of tzatziki drizzled with olive oil, with grilled pitta and crudités alongside

ingredients.name: grated cucumber (about 1 medium cucumber, unpeeled, grated on the large holes of a box grater)

steps: Working with one handful at a time, squeeze the grated cucumber between your palms over the sink to wring out the water. Put the squeezed cucumber in a bowl.
Add the yogurt, olive oil, herbs, lemon juice, garlic and salt and stir to combine. Let it sit for 5 minutes so the flavours meld, then taste and add more herbs, lemon or salt if it needs it.
Serve straight away or chill. It keeps in the fridge for about 4 days.

title: Red lentil curry
blurb: Slow-cooked onions and carrots, red lentils and coconut milk. One pot, pantry staples.
description: A simple, deeply savoury curry from pantry staples: onions and carrots cooked slowly until sweet, curry powder, a tin of tomatoes, a tin of coconut milk and a handful of red lentils that melt into the sauce. Vegan, one pot, and better the next day. Serve with rice or flatbreads.
imageAlt: A bowl of orange red lentil curry topped with parsley, with the pot and a dish of dried lentils beside it

ingredients.name: medium onion, halved and thinly sliced
sea salt, plus more to taste

steps: Heat a large pot over low to medium heat. Add the oil and onions and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and lightly browned. If they brown too fast, lower the heat and add a splash of water.
Add the carrots, garlic and ginger and cook for another 10 minutes. The carrots should soften but not cook through.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for a minute.

Add the tomatoes, coconut milk and salt. Swill the tomato tin with about 60ml of water and add that too. Bring to a strong simmer, stir in the lentils, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the lentils are cooked.
Taste, season, and serve hot with whatever toppings or sides you like.

title: Avocado toast
blurb: Crisp toast, mashed avocado with lemon and salt, a fried egg on top if you like.
description: The ten-minute breakfast: bread toasted until properly crisp, a ripe avocado mashed with lemon juice and salt so it keeps some texture, then chilli flakes and a thread of olive oil. Add a fried or poached egg to make it a meal.
imageAlt: Avocado toast topped with a fried egg, basil leaves and everything seasoning on a white plate
steps: Toast the bread until deeply golden and crisp.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and salt, leaving some texture.
Spread the avocado thickly over the toast.
Top with a fried or poached egg if using, and finish with chili flakes and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Vegetable omelette
blurb: Three eggs, pepper, mushroom and spinach, folded over melted cheese. Ten minutes.
description: A soft, fluffy omelette for one. The vegetables are softened first so the eggs cook fast over gentle heat, then the pan is tilted so the raw egg runs underneath and the omelette folds over cheese while the top is still barely set.
imageAlt: A folded omelette with melted cheese and chives on a white plate with lettuce and tomato
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper until fully blended.
Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat and soften the pepper and mushrooms for about 3 minutes. Add the spinach to wilt, then tip the vegetables out onto a plate.
Melt the rest of the butter and pour in the eggs, swirling to coat the pan.
As the edges set, lift them with a spatula and tilt the pan so the raw egg runs underneath.
When the top is just barely set, scatter the vegetables and cheese over one half, fold the other half over, and slide onto a plate.

title: Balsamic roasted vegetables
blurb: Sweet potato, peppers and broccoli roasted hot, then glazed with balsamic. A week of sides in one tray.
description: A big tray of roasted vegetables for the week: sweet potato gets a head start in a hot oven, peppers and broccoli join later, and a splash of balsamic at the end glazes everything as it finishes browning. Eat them warm as a side or cold on salads. Vegan and gluten-free.
imageAlt: Roasted sweet potato, broccoli and red and green peppers piled on a speckled plate with a serving spoon

ingredients.name: sweet potato (1 large or 2 small), cut into 3cm cubes

steps: Heat the oven to 230°C and grease a large baking tray.
Toss the sweet potato cubes in a large bowl with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and ½ tsp of the garlic salt. Spread on the tray and roast for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring once, until starting to brown.
Meanwhile toss the peppers and broccoli in the same bowl with the remaining 2 tbsp oil and ½ tsp garlic salt. Add other spices if you like: garlic powder, onion powder, Italian seasoning.
Add the peppers and broccoli to the tray, stir everything together and roast for 10 minutes more, until they start to soften.
Drizzle the balsamic over the tray and stir to coat. Roast for a final 10 to 15 minutes, stirring halfway, until nicely browned.
Serve warm as a side, or cool and keep in the fridge for salads through the week.

title: Tomato and egg cottage cheese pot
blurb: Oregano-marinated cherry tomatoes, cottage cheese, cucumber and a jammy egg in a jar. Prep the night before.
description: Cherry tomatoes marinated in oregano and olive oil until they release their juices, which become the dressing, layered in a jar with cool cottage cheese, crunchy cucumber and a seven-minute egg, then basil torn over the top. Eat it straight away or keep it sealed in the fridge for a couple of days.
imageAlt: A white bowl of cottage cheese, halved jammy eggs, cherry tomatoes, cucumber and basil
steps: Halve the cherry tomatoes and toss them in a bowl with the oregano, olive oil and a generous pinch of salt and pepper. Leave to marinate for at least 15 minutes: they soften and release their juices, which become the dressing. Use the ripest tomatoes you can find.
Meanwhile bring a small pan of water to the boil, lower in the egg and cook for 7 minutes, then cool it in cold water. Peel and halve. Slice the cucumber into half-moons.

Spoon the tomatoes and all their juices into the base of a jar or pot. Add a layer of cottage cheese, then the cucumber. Top with the egg halves, tear over the basil and finish with a last pinch of salt and pepper.
Eat straight away, or seal and keep in the fridge for up to 2 days.

title: Parmesan asparagus with poached eggs
blurb: Blanched asparagus grilled under a crust of parmesan, a poached egg on top, toast on the side.
description: Simple and elegant: thick asparagus blanched until just tender, brushed with butter, showered with Parmigiano-Reggiano and flashed under the grill, then topped with a poached egg cooked in the same water. Break the yolk over the spears and mop it up with toast.
imageAlt: Two fried eggs with chilli flakes and herbs on a bed of roasted asparagus spears

ingredients.name: salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps: Heat the grill to high. Blanch the asparagus in a large, deep pan of boiling salted water until just tender, about 3 minutes. Lift out with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper and pat dry. Keep the water in the pan.

Arrange the asparagus in four shallow ovenproof dishes, brush with the butter and season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle over the cheese and grill about 15cm from the heat until golden, about 1 minute.
Add the vinegar to the asparagus water and bring back to a simmer. Crack in the eggs with plenty of space between them and poach until the whites are set and the yolks still runny, about 3 minutes.
Lift each egg out with a slotted spoon, blot dry on kitchen paper and set on the asparagus. Serve with toast.

title: Creamy lemon garlic salmon pasta
blurb: Seared salmon flaked through egg pasta in a lemon, garlic and parmesan cream sauce.
description: Salmon seared in olive oil and flaked into ribbons of egg pasta coated in a sauce of butter, onion, garlic, chicken stock and cream, sharpened with lemon juice and zest and thickened with Parmigiano-Reggiano. The caption only listed the ingredients; the method here is how it goes together in the video.
imageAlt: Tongs lifting creamy tagliatelle with flakes of seared salmon and chopped parsley
steps: Season the salmon all over with the salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and sear the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes a side until golden and just cooked through. Lift onto a plate and flake into big pieces, discarding the skin.
Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Save a mugful of the cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile, in the same frying pan, melt the butter over medium heat and soften the onion for 4 to 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for a minute more.
Pour in the chicken stock and let it bubble for 2 minutes, then add the cream, lemon juice and zest and the salt. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Stir in the parmesan until melted, then add the pasta and toss to coat, loosening with pasta water as needed. Fold in the flaked salmon gently so it stays in pieces and serve at once.

title: Georgian salad
blurb: Tomato, cucumber and red onion in a walnut, garlic and blue fenugreek dressing.
description: The tomato and cucumber salad from every Georgian table, in its walnut version: the walnuts are blended with garlic, lemon juice, Kakhetian oil, coriander and utskho suneli into a thick dressing that clings to the vegetables. Kakhetian oil is unrefined sunflower oil; utskho suneli is blue fenugreek. Both are worth finding, but ordinary sunflower oil and a pinch of ground fenugreek will get you close.
imageAlt: A plate of tomato, cucumber and red onion salad coated in a crumbly walnut dressing with herbs

ingredients.name: fresh herbs: coriander, basil or parsley

steps: Wash the vegetables. Cut the cucumbers and tomatoes into the size you like, cubes or half-moons, and slice the onion into thin half-rings.
Make the dressing: put the walnuts, utskho suneli, garlic, lemon juice, Kakhetian oil, the coriander and salt in a food processor and blend to a smooth paste.
Put the chopped vegetables and the finely chopped herbs in a bowl, add the walnut dressing, the basil and the onion, and toss to coat. Taste for salt and pepper.

title: Carrot cake overnight oats
blurb: Oats, yogurt and grated carrot with cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg. Tastes like cake, counts as breakfast.
description: Carrot cake flavours in a jar of overnight oats: grated carrot, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg stirred into oats, Greek yogurt and milk, with raisins for sweetness and walnuts on top for crunch. Make two jars the night before and breakfast is done. Swap the yogurt and milk for plant-based ones to keep it vegan.
imageAlt: A glass jar of carrot cake overnight oats with raisins and cinnamon, a gold spoon standing in it

ingredients.name: walnuts or pecans, chopped, to serve

steps: Whisk the yogurt, milk, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg in a large bowl until smooth. It should look light brown.
Stir in the grated carrot and raisins, then the oats, mixing until everything is coated.
Cover the bowl or divide between jars and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight, so the oats soften.
In the morning, stir. Loosen with a splash of milk if it is too thick. Eat cold or warm briefly in the microwave, topped with the walnuts, a drizzle of maple syrup and a sprinkle of cinnamon.

title: Ultimate carbonara
blurb: No cream, lots of black pepper: egg yolks, smoked bacon, two cheeses and starchy pasta water, plus a little garlic.
description: Mob's take on the classic, and there is no cream anywhere near it. Egg yolks are whisked with grated pecorino, parmesan and a very generous amount of black pepper, crisp smoked bacon and sliced garlic wait in the pan, and the drained spaghetti is tossed through with ladles of starchy pasta water until it turns silky. Crack the eggs into a separate bowl first, keep the whites for meringue, and if it looks thick add more pasta water: it should be smooth, not scrambled.
imageAlt: Tongs lifting a tangle of creamy carbonara spaghetti flecked with bacon out of a black frying pan

ingredients.name: egg yolks (freeze the whites for meringue)
parmesan, plus a little to serve
black pepper, freshly cracked, lots of it

steps: Grate the pecorino and parmesan into a bowl, setting a pinch of parmesan aside for serving. Add the egg yolks and a very generous amount of black pepper (a good carbonara is peppery, hence the name) and whisk together.
Chop the bacon into small pieces and fry in a large pan over a medium heat until crisp.
Meanwhile cook the spaghetti in a large pan of well-salted boiling water: pasta water should taste almost as salty as the sea.
Add the sliced garlic to the crisp bacon and let it soften. If anything starts to catch, add a spoonful of the starchy pasta water.

A minute before the pasta is ready, while still quite al dente, ladle out some pasta water (about 1½ ladles per person) into a bowl. Drain the pasta and tip it into the bacon pan with about ½ a ladle of pasta water per person. Cook together over a medium heat until the water has evaporated and the pasta is silky, then take off the heat.

Let it cool for 1 minute, then add the egg and cheese mixture with another ½ ladle of pasta water per person and mix well. If it looks too thick, add a little more water: it should be silky smooth. Serve with the reserved parmesan and a twist or two more of black pepper.

title: Hummus
blurb: Silky hummus from a jar of chickpeas, tahini, cumin and lemon, blitzed with the chickpea liquid and finished with olive oil and za’atar.
description: Mob's silky hummus, and the trick is what goes in the blender: a whole jar of chickpeas with their liquid, tahini, a little garlic, cumin and lemon, blitzed until completely smooth. The olive oil is not blended in but poured over at the end, which is what keeps it light, and the best chickpeas and extra virgin olive oil you can find make a real difference. It keeps for 3 to 5 days in the fridge.
imageAlt: A speckled bowl of swirled hummus topped with olive oil, whole chickpeas and za’atar, a hand dipping a piece of bread into it

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil, to serve

steps: Pour the liquid from the top of the chickpea jar into a jug, then tip the chickpeas and the rest of their liquid into a blender or food processor. Add the tahini, finely grate in the garlic if using, and add the cumin and the juice of half the lemon.
Blitz until silky smooth. If it is still a little coarse, add some of the reserved chickpea liquid and blitz again. Season to taste with salt, pepper and more lemon juice.
Spoon into a bowl, top with a generous drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkling of za’atar, and serve with everything.

title: Healthy cheesecake
blurb: Four ingredients and no crust: Greek yogurt, eggs, honey and vanilla whisked in one bowl, baked until just set and chilled overnight.
description: A crustless cheesecake made from thick Greek yogurt, eggs, honey and vanilla: whisk in one bowl, bake until the edges are set and the middle still wobbles, then cool and chill for at least four hours (overnight is better). It sets to a smooth, custardy slice with a good amount of protein and no refined sugar. Use thick yogurt, not a watery one, and do not overbake. Fold in a handful of blueberries or add lemon zest to the batter if you like; it keeps for 4 to 5 days in the fridge, and slices freeze for a month.
imageAlt: A baked cheesecake with a caramelised top on a glass cake stand, one slice cut out to show the creamy inside

ingredients.name: honey and fresh berries, to serve (optional)

steps: Heat the oven to 170°C. Line an 18cm round tin with baking parchment, covering the base and sides.
Whisk the yogurt, eggs, honey and vanilla in a large bowl until completely smooth, with no streaks of egg left.
Pour into the tin and tap it on the counter a few times to knock out the large air bubbles.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre still has a slight wobble. It firms up as it cools, so do not bake it until the middle is solid.
Cool completely in the tin at room temperature, then chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight for the best texture.
Slice while cold and serve with a drizzle of honey and a few berries.
